intro.title: Implement DeepReadonly type
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a TypeScript type called DeepReadonly that makes all properties of an object—including nested objects—immutable (read-only). You will learn how to use mapped types and conditional types to recursively traverse and transform object structures. The main technologies involved are TypeScript's type system features like keyof, readonly, and recursive type definitions. By the end, you will understand how to create utility types that enforce immutability at any depth, a key concept for type safety in larger applications.
intro.usecase: The DeepReadonly type is essential in TypeScript applications where you need to guarantee data immutability for safety and predictability. In real-world products like configuration dashboards or admin panels, you often fetch complex nested data structures (user profiles with nested permissions, organizational hierarchies, or multi-level settings objects) that should never be accidentally modified by UI components. By applying DeepReadonly to these data structures, you prevent runtime mutations that could cause inconsistent UI states or bugs, while still allowing TypeScript to provide full type safety and autocomplete during development. This pattern is particularly valuable in React applications with state management libraries, where immutable state updates are required for proper re-rendering and performance optimization.
